Warren County Fiscal Court
Meeting Minutes
August 13, 2026
Pursuant to adjournment, Warren Fiscal Court met on Thursday, August 13, 2026
at 9:00 AM in the Warren County Fiscal Courtroom at 429 E 10th Avenue, Bowling
Green, Kentucky. Present were: Esquire Eric Aldridge, Esquire Ron Cummings,
Esquire Scott Lasley, Esquire Tom Lawrence, and Esquire Rick Williams. Presiding
Judge Executive Doug Gorman. Absent: Esquire Rex McWhorter
**********
Invocation by Pastor Lonnie Winston, Miracle Life Church.
**********
Esquire Williams led the pledge to the flag.
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve minutes of the
Fiscal Court meeting on July 30, 2026. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays,
one absent. It is so ordered. (4)
**********
Esquire Aldridge moved, seconded by Esquire Cummings to approve personnel
changes for Warren County. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one
absent. It is so ordered. (5)
**********
Esquire Aldridge moved, seconded by Esquire Cummings to approve work schedule
for the Warren County Road Department. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no
nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (6)
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Aldridge to approve second and
final reading of Ordinance #26-19WC Rezoning property located at 5488, 5538, and
5558 Scottsville Road from AG (Agriculture) and GB (General Business) to HB
(Highway business) containing approximately 2.20 acres and presently owned by
Josh Baker; Jeff & Valerie Powell; and Tristan & Kamrin Summer Adams. Upon
roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (See Fiscal
Court Order Book 21, Supp. 240, 570-A). (8)
**********
Proponents and Opponents regarding the following rezoning
ordinance (#26-13WC) were allowed to give public comment.
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve Ordinance #26-
18WC Rezoning property located at Dillard Road, 380 Feet East of Station Drive
and Abutting Mount Forbes Drive to the North from AG (Agriculture) to RS-1B
(Single Family Residential) containing approximately 34.865 acres and presently
owned by Thomas R. Hunt Investment Properties, LLC. Upon roll call the vote was:
five yeas, one nay, one absent. It is so ordered. (See Fiscal Court Order Book 21,
Supp. 240, 571-A). (7)
**********
Esquire Lasley moved, seconded by Esquire Lawrence to approve emergency
determination in the amount of $46,665 to Stewart Richey Service Group for
emergency repair of collapsed drain lines at the jail in the A-unit hallway, kitchen,
and the A-overflow cell. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It
is so ordered. (9)
**********
Esquire Lasley moved, seconded by Esquire Lawrence to approve emergency
determination in the amount of $8,975 to Trane, Inc. for replacement of an AC
compressor at the jail. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is
so ordered. (10)
**********
Esquire Aldridge moved, seconded by Esquire Cummings to approve quarterly
financial report from Woodburn Fire Department. Upon roll call the vote was: six
yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (11)
**********
Esquire Williams moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve lease agreement
with Enterprise Fleet for (2) 2027 Dodge Durangos for the Parks Department in an
amount not to exceed $850 per month each for 60 months. (Contracted Vendor).
Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (12)
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve lease agreement
with Enterprise Fleet for (2) 2027 F-350s to replace (2) F-350s with expiring leases
for the Parks Department in an amount not to exceed $1,250 per month each for 60
months. (Contracted Vendor). Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one
absent. It is so ordered. (13)
**********
Esquire Aldridge moved, seconded by Esquire Cummings to approve emergency
determination in the amount of $3,150 to Stewart Richey Service Group for
emergency plumbing repair in cell A-1 at the jail. Upon roll call the vote was: six
yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (14)
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve determination in
the amount of $16,000 for a 3-year subscription renewal with Turf Tank for the
robotic field painting machine for Parks. (Contracted Vendor). Upon roll call the
vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (15)
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve Memorandum of
Agreement with SKYCTC for partnership on the SKYRISE Program at no cost to
Warren County to allow eligible inmates to participate in college course work while
incarcerated and authorize Jailer to sign all related documents. Upon roll call the
vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (16)
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve 2-1-1 Report for
July 2026. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered.
(17)
**********
Esquire Aldridge moved, seconded by Esquire Cummings to approve second and
final reading of Ordinance #26-20WC Establishing the Warren County Department
of Public Safety and Providing for The Administration of Fire Protection and
Emergency Management Services. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one
absent. It is so ordered. (See Fiscal Court Order Book 21, Supp. 240, 572-A-3). (18)
**********
Esquire Cummings moved, seconded by Esquire Aldridge to approve 1-year
agreement in the amount of $50,000 between Goodwill Another Way and Warren
County Solid Waste. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is
so ordered. (19)
**********
Esquire Aldridge moved, seconded by Esquire Cummings to approve determination
in the amount of $34,900 to Gary Force Honda for the purchase of a 2026 Honda
CRV for Drug Taskforce. (Paid for with funds from the DTF auction at no cost to
Warren County). Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so
ordered. (20)
**********
Esquire Aldridge moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve lease agreement
with Enterprise Fleet for a 2026 Chevrolet Silverado 2500 in an amount not to
exceed $1100 per month for 60 months for the Department of Public Safety. Upon
roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (21)
**********
Esquire Lasley moved, seconded by Esquire Lawrence to approve Order #26-32
Declaring Surplus Property (Vehicle for the Jail). Upon roll call the vote was: six
yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (See Fiscal Court Order Book 21, Supp.
240, 572-B). (22)
**********
Esquire Cummings moved, seconded by Esquire Aldridge to approve first reading
of Ordinance #26-21WC Establishing Trenton Lane, Annapolis Lane, and Topeka
Road, Located in Carter Crossings Subdivision, Phase 4 as County Roads and
Authorizing Maintenance Thereon & Setting Speed Limits Thereon. Upon roll call
the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (23)
**********
Esquire Williams moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve determination in
the amount of $13,324 to PennCare for the purchase of four (4) AEDs for vehicles
for the Department of Public Safety. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays,
one absent. It is so ordered. (24)
**********
Esquire Aldridge moved, seconded by Esquire Lawrence to approve interfund
transfers for Warren County. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one
absent. It is so ordered. (25)
**********
Esquire Lasley moved, seconded by Esquire Lawrence to approve budget transfers
for Warren County. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is
so ordered. (26)
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Lasley to approve Order #26-33
Declaring Surplus Equipment for Parks and Rec. Upon roll call the vote was: six
yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (See Fiscal Court Order Book 21, Supp.
240, 573-A). (27)
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Williams to grant authority to
advertise for the parks vending machine bid. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas,
no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (28)
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Williams to grant authority to
advertise for bids for portable toilets, hand washing stations, and grease cleaning for
parks. Upon roll call the vote was: six yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (29)
**********
Esquire Aldridge moved, seconded by Esquire Cummings to approve determination
in the amount of $3,850 to Stripes and More for window tinting at the Training
Center at Sugar Maple Square. (Best evaluated bid). Upon roll call the vote was: six
yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (30)
**********
Magistrates present were given a copy of claims to be paid and after examination of
all claims the following motion was made: Esquire Cummings moved seconded by
Esquire Aldridge to approve claims as submitted. Upon roll call the vote was: six
yeas, no nays, one absent. It is so ordered. (31)
**********
Esquire Lawrence moved, seconded by Esquire Aldridge that court adjourn to meet
again on Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 9:00 AM. It is so ordered.
______________________________________
DOUGLAS J. GORMAN
WARREN COUNTY JUDGE EXECUTIVE
